title: Deadline-aware slot reservation and probabilistic tail-gating for continual batching
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Background: Continuous batching reduces per-token cost but exposes services to sporadic tail-latency spikes when a few long requests or bursty arrivals contend for KV/prefill resources. Current admission logic is reactive and tends to either over-throttle (hurting throughput) or under-protect (causing 95/99p latency regressions).

Goal: Implement a deadline-aware slot reservation layer combined with a probabilistic tail-gating mechanism to smooth bursts and bound tail latencies without sacrificing steady-state throughput. The feature should integrate with kernel-selection hints so the admission layer can prefer kernel-friendly batch shapes when under stress, and age prefill requests so in-progress prefill work isn't wasted by aggressive admission.

Scope: This ticket covers design and implementation of the admission/reservation algorithm, runtime hooks for kernel-selection hints, telemetry additions (per-slot occupancy, reservation misses, gated admissions), and an A/B test in canary fleet. It does not include RBAC UI or billing implications (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Implemented slot reservation API (soft reservations) with configurable deadlines and decay parameters
Probabilistic tail-gating reduces 99th percentile prefill+decode latency by >=25% in our staging workload without >5% throughput regression
Kernel-selection receives batch-shape hints when reservations are active and produces compatible choices (verified by unit tests)
Observability: dashboards for reservation utilization, gated-admissions, and per-tenant tail events are populated
Canary rollout pipeline and automated rollback on latency regressions are in place
design_notes: Slot model: maintain N logical slots per GPU (configurable per pool). Each incoming request obtains either: immediate slot, soft-reservation (temporary promise), or is probabilistically gated based on current load and request deadline.

Reservation semantics: soft-reservations reduce unnecessary prefill work by reserving a future timeslice for a decode without burning kernel context. Reservations decay if not used within reservation_ttl and are preferentially assigned to shorter-deadline requests.

Probabilistic tail-gating: under congestion, calculate gate probability p = min(1, alpha * (queue_depth - threshold) / capacity). Requests that lose the coinflip drop to a low-cost fallback (smaller model or cached response) or return 429 depending on SLA tier.

Deadline buckets: classify requests into latency buckets (low: <50ms, medium: 50-200ms, high: >200ms). Higher-priority buckets get reservation preference; longer-deadline requests can be steered to batched prefill windows to increase kernel efficiency.

Kernel hints: admission layer emits batch-shape hints (e.g., expected sequence lengths, token counts) so kernel-selector can prefer kernels optimized for the projected shape. This helps avoid expensive kernel swaps during decode.

Prefill aging: if a prefill has been running and the request misses admission, mark the prefill with 'keep-on-miss' until either decode starts or a short grace timer expires to avoid wasted computation. Grace window tuned experimentally.
Configuration knobs: reservation_ttl, slot_count_per_device, gate_alpha, gate_threshold, grace_window_ms, bucket_thresholds, fallback_policy
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype slot table and basic soft-reservation flow in a test harness (2 days)
Integrate reservation state into admission controller; add gate probability calculation and simple fallback paths (4 days)
Expose kernel-shape hint interface and wire through to kernel selector (3 days)
Implement prefill aging flag and grace timer in prefill worker (2 days)
Add telemetry counters, traces, and Grafana dashboard panels (2 days)
Run cluster-scale perf tests and iterate thresholds (5 days)
Canary rollout and monitoring for 2 weeks with rollback criteria (auto rollback on 99p latency > baseline+15%)
milestones: 2026-03-15: Admission controller integrated and unit tests added
2026-03-22: Kernel hinting wired; perf test run #1
risks: Reserved slots could be held by slow tenants causing head-of-line blocking — mitigated via reservation_ttl and tenant fairness scoring
Probabilistic gating may increase error rates for latency-sensitive customers — plan to implement tiered fallback policies and opt-outs for enterprise customers
Kernel hint mismatch could cause more kernel swaps and regressions — require conservative hinting and fallback to baseline selector
Telemetry volume increases; dashboards must be sampled and aggregated to avoid SLI noise
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservation table correctness, TTL expiry, and gating RNG determinism
Integration test with prefill + decode pipeline: simulate mixed short/long sequences and validate prefill aging behavior
Perf tests: compare baseline vs feature under Poisson and bursty arrival patterns using synthetic traces and real production replay (from ENG-27503 and ENG-31247 datasets)
Canary experiment: 10% of capacity for two weeks with A/B buckets, automated rollback on SLA breach
Chaos: inject slow GPU kernels and verify reservation decay avoids head-of-line blocking
perf_targets: 99th percentile end-to-end prefill+decode latency: -25% vs baseline under bursty load
Average throughput degradation: <=5% under steady load
Reservation utilization: >=70% when load is >75% of provisioned capacity
